title: Devin turns production failure traces into evals, lifting Rox's coverage from 43% to 72%
summary: Rox's team found their agents shipped faster than people could write tests. They set up Devin to pull failing production traces from Braintrust, recreate each failure in a preview environment and turn it into an eval case.
agent_role: Devin pulls production traces, reproduces each failure in a preview environment and writes it up as an eval. The team designed the loop.
outcome: The author reports eval suite coverage rising from 43% to 72%, and still climbing.
what_they_did: Rox's applied AI team built a loop around Devin. Devin pulls production traces from Braintrust and rebuilds each failure in a preview environment. It then converts the failure into an eval for their agent test suite.
how_it_went: The author says eval coverage went from 43% to 72% and is still growing.
worth_knowing: The post gives no detail on how evals are reviewed or how flaky reproductions are handled. It is also partly a hiring announcement.
prompt: Pull the last [number] failed traces from [observability tool, e.g. Braintrust] for [project]. For each one, reproduce the failure in a preview environment of [repo URL]. Then write an eval case that captures the expected correct behaviour, using our existing eval format in [eval folder]. Group duplicates together. Show me the list of proposed evals with the trace each came from, and wait for my approval before opening a PR.

curation.rationale: A genuine and fairly original loop: Devin turns production failures into evals, with a reported coverage number. Evidence is a short post that is partly a hiring pitch, and there is little detail on setup.
